title: Geometry of affine-source Cech nerves over qcqs stacks
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $T$ and $V$ be affine $S$-schemes, and let $h:\mathcal A\to T$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated morphism of algebraic stacks over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Let $v:V\to\mathcal A$ be any morphism; it need not be smooth or surjective. For $p\geq0$ form $V_p=V\times_{\mathcal A}\cdots\times_{\mathcal A}V$ with $p+1$ factors and augmentation $v_p:V_p\to\mathcal A$, using [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Then $V_p$ is representable by an algebraic space [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $h\circ v_p:V_p\to T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. If $\mathcal A$ is representable by an algebraic space, every $V_p$ is representable by a scheme. If $\mathcal A$ is representable by a scheme $A$, every $V_p$ is a scheme separated over $T$, meaning its relative diagonal over $T$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. If, in addition, $A\to T$ is separated, every $V_p$ is affine. These assertions hold for the empty schemes and for $p=0$; no finite-type or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 076Z, lemma-general-pushforward, proof paragraphs 2--5: geometry of iterated affine-source fibre products. Quasi-compact and quasi-separated fibre products: stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 075S, lemma-quasi-compact-quasi-separated-permanence, (2),(3).

proof.text: We may regard the stacks and spaces as absolute objects, retaining their maps to $S$ and $T$: [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-change-base-to-integers] preserves the relevant fibre products and relative qcqs predicates, without any separation hypothesis on $S$. Put $Q=V\times_TV$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] the morphism $V\to T$ between affine schemes is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a ring map, so the affine tensor-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] makes $Q$ affine. Thus $V,T,Q$ are quasi-compact and absolutely quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The morphisms $V\to T$ and both projections $Q\to V$ are separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated].

source.place: Tag 076Z, proof, affine-base reduction and the four diagonal reductions; affine fibre products: schemes.tex Tag 01JQ.

proof.text: Put $R=V\times_{\mathcal A}V$. There is a cartesian square with top arrow $R\to\mathcal A$, bottom arrow $Q\to\mathcal A\times_T\mathcal A$ induced by $(v,v)$, and right arrow $\Delta_h$. Indeed, on each test scheme an object of its pullback is a pair of maps to $V$ and an isomorphism between their images in $\mathcal A$; its image in the discrete groupoid $T$ is the identity. This is precisely the defining $2$-fibre product. By the quasi-separatedness clause of [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism], its scheme test $r:R\to Q$ is an algebraic space morphism that is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Since $Q$ is quasi-compact, taking the identity test $Q\to Q$ in the definition of a quasi-compact space morphism shows that $R$ is quasi-compact. Since $Q$ is absolutely quasi-separated and $r$ is quasi-separated, [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] shows that $R$ is absolutely quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 076Z, proof paragraph beginning "In this situation"; relative-diagonal test made explicit; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04ZH (2).

proof.text: Let $a,b:R\to V$ be the two projections. Define $W_0=V$, and for $p\geq1$ define $W_p$ as $p$ copies of $R$ fibred over $V$, matching $b$ of one copy with $a$ of the next. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] these are algebraic spaces. On a test scheme a point of $W_p$ consists of $x_0,\ldots,x_p$ in $V$ and consecutive isomorphisms $v(x_{i-1})\simeq v(x_i)$. Composing them identifies this groupoid with the $p+1$-fold $2$-product defining $V_p$; conversely the isomorphisms to the first object give consecutive ones by taking inverses and composing. These operations are inverse, including on arrows, and commute with pullback. Hence $W_p\simeq V_p$. Starting with the qcqs objects $V$ and $R$, the fibre-product clause of [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products], applied at each step over the qcqs space $V$, proves by induction that every $W_p$ is qcqs.

source.place: Tag 076Z, proof, displayed iterated fibre products; spaces.tex Tag 02X2 and spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 073B (3).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-qcqs-permanence] to $W_p\to T$. Its source is qcqs and its target is quasi-separated by Steps 1--3. Here the algebraic-space and stack absolute separation conventions agree directly: the diagonal of a sheaf is a monomorphism, whose own diagonal is an isomorphism, so its extra quasi-separatedness as a representable stack map imposes no additional condition. Likewise a quasi-compact etale scheme atlas is a quasi-compact smooth scheme atlas, since every etale morphism of schemes is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres]. Thus the lemma gives that $W_p\to T$, and therefore $h\circ v_p$, is quasi-compact and quasi-separated in the required stack sense. No assumption about smoothness or surjectivity of $v$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 076Z, proof, qcqs assertion; stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 075S (2).

proof.text: If $\mathcal A$ is an algebraic space, its diagonal is representable by schemes by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Pull it back along $V\times_SV\to\mathcal A\times_S\mathcal A$: the resulting scheme represents $R$. This follows on test objects from the same pair-and-isomorphism description as in Step 2, with the groupoids now discrete. The recursion $W_p=W_{p-1}\times_VR$ is therefore a recursion using scheme fibre products, which exist by [def-pc-fibre-product]. It follows by induction from $W_0=V$ that every $V_p$ is represented by a scheme.

source.place: Tag 076Z, proof, algebraic-space reduction: "the diagonal of an algebraic space is representable by schemes".

proof.text: Now suppose $\mathcal A$ is a scheme $A$. Then $R$ and every $W_p$ are schemes directly: on test schemes $h_V\times_{h_A}h_V$ is represented by the scheme fibre product $V\times_AV$ of [def-pc-fibre-product], and the recursion $W_p=W_{p-1}\times_VR$ of Step 5 uses only scheme fibre products. The square of Step 2 identifies $r:R\to Q$ with a scheme base change of $\Delta_{A/T}$. The diagonal is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-diagonal-immersion], so $r$ is an immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft]. Each $Q\to V$ is separated by Step 1. Therefore [lem-trf-immersion-over-separated-base] makes $a,b:R\to V$ separated. In the recursion of Step 3 the projection $W_p\to W_{p-1}$ is a base change of $a$ (use the last projection $W_{p-1}\to V$ and attach the next copy of $R$). It is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change]. With the separated base case $W_0=V\to T$ of Step 1, composition of separated morphisms in [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] proves inductively that $W_p\to T$ is separated. This is exactly the assertion that its relative diagonal is a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 076Z, proof, scheme reduction; schemes.tex Tags 01KJ, 01JY, 01L8 and 01KU.

proof.text: If in addition $A\to T$ is separated, its diagonal is a closed immersion by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] its pullback $r:R\to Q$ is a closed immersion. Taking the whole affine target $Q$ in the affine description of [def-weil-closed-immersion] shows that $R$ is affine. The recursion $W_p=W_{p-1}\times_VR$ now involves only affine schemes over the affine scheme $V$, so [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] proves their affineness inductively. For $p=0$ all claims are the affine scheme $V$ and its morphism to affine $T$ from Step 1. If $V$ or $T$ is empty, the constructions and the same identities still apply (the empty affine is the spectrum of the zero ring); none of the cited results requires nonemptiness, finite type, or Noetherian hypotheses.

lean.statement: theorem stack_affine_source_nerve_geometry {S : Scheme.{u}} (T V : Over S) [IsAffine T.left] [IsAffine V.left] (A : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hA : IsAlgebraicModuliStack A) (h : BasedFunctor A (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj T))) (hhqc : IsQuasiCompactAlgebraicModuliMap.{u, v, w, u, u + 1, t, s} h) (hhqs : IsQuasiSeparatedAlgebraicModuliMap h) (a : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj V)) A) (p : ℕ) : (∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (e : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli Z.obj.obj) (stackAffineSourceNerve a p).1), e.toFunctor.IsEquivalence) ∧ IsQuasiCompactAlgebraicModuliMap.{u, max u v, max (u + 1) v w, u, u + 1, t, s} ((stackAffineSourceNerve a p).2.comp h) ∧ IsQuasiSeparatedAlgebraicModuliMap ((stackAffineSourceNerve a p).2.comp h) ∧ ((∃ (Z : AlgebraicSpace S) (e : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli Z.obj.obj) A), e.toFunctor.IsEquivalence) → ∃ W : Over S, IsRepresentedByScheme (stackAffineSourceNerve a p).1 W) ∧ (∀ (B : Over S) (e : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj B)) A), e.toFunctor.IsEquivalence → ∀ b : B ⟶ T, Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (e.comp h) (discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map b))) → ∃ (W : Over S) (q : W ⟶ T) (f : BasedFunctor (discreteModuli (yoneda.obj W)) (stackAffineSourceNerve a p).1), f.toFunctor.IsEquivalence ∧ Nonempty (ModuliTwoIso (f.comp ((stackAffineSourceNerve a p).2.comp h)) (discreteModuliMap (yoneda.map q))) ∧ IsClosedImmersion (pullback.diagonal q.left) ∧ (IsSeparated b.left → IsAffine W.left))
